author: Sahil Kurup
title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's savage act after scoring on Dillon Brooks in NBA Playoffs payback - NewsBreak
text:
By Sahil Kurup ,
1 hours ago Dillon Brooks had a message for the Oklahoma City Thunder before the first-round series even began.
Fresh off Phoenix 's play-in win over Golden State, still dripping in sweat, Brooks delivered an unprompted broadside at the defending champions. "There are a lot of foul baiters on that team," he told the Amazon Prime crew. "I hope it's the real playoffs. They call too many calls. Show your hands."
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander heard him. And on Wednesday night in Game 2 at Paycom Center, with the Thunder up five and five minutes left in the second quarter, the reigning NBA MVP delivered his response, not in words, but in a pull-up midrange jumper straight over Brooks' outstretched hand, followed by a deliberate point directly at his defender as a wide grin appeared on his face. Meanwhile, Brooks earned an unlikely $1 million bonus after crushing Steph Curry's playoff hopes.

The sequence unfolded naturally out of the game's early tension. Brooks had been playing with his characteristic aggression, hounding Gilgeous-Alexander throughout the first half and forcing a miss on a contested attempt in the second quarter before barking in his direction.
It was exactly the kind of defensive intensity Brooks had promised, following the scout, showing hands, funneling toward the paint. For a few possessions, it worked.
Then Gilgeous-Alexander reset, caught a clean look off the dribble, and buried it, and the point at Brooks afterward landed with all the weight of a man who had been keeping receipts.
Brooks, who averaged 20.2 points this season in a career year that helped transform the Suns' culture, has never been shy about turning playoff series into personal battles.
Gilgeous-Alexander had arrived at Game 2 already having demonstrated that physical adversity was not going to slow him down.
He tweaked a finger on his shooting hand early in the first quarter after taking an accidental kick to the hand as he fell to the floor, wincing and gripping the hand repeatedly while refusing to come out of the game.
He played all twelve first-quarter minutes and finished the period with 11 points on five of nine shooting, leading all scorers.
The Thunder had taken Game 1 by 35 points, with Gilgeous-Alexander scoring 25 and Oklahoma City running up 34 points off 19 Suns turnovers.
Phoenix has now lost seven straight playoff games dating back to 2023. But Game 2 was considerably tighter through the first half, until a third-quarter explosion from Chet Holmgren opened the floodgates.
Jalen Williams picked up the offensive slack through stretches, scoring 16 first-half points, while Jalen Green, who had erupted for 35 and 36 in Phoenix's two play-in victories, found his footing with 12 in the second quarter after a quiet opening frame.
